items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: Recommended for Raid. Font of Venomous Rage is a powerful burst damage trinket providing massive on-use single-target damage on a long 4-minute cooldown. This trinket can be obtained at item level 344 from Mythic Ula'tek and is currently the strongest trinket available for pure Single Target, particularly if burst damage is valuable or required. That said, this trinket does not scale as well as stat trinkets when it comes to buffing allies in sustained AoE encounters, and there are few encounters in Season 2 with a pure single-target damage profile.

items.name: Mindpiercer's Sigil
items.guideNote: Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Mindpiercer's Sigil is a passive trinket with no baseline stats, instead providing direct damage and an Intellect proc. This trinket loses some value in high target counts, but on average is one of the strongest trinkets available for Augmentation in Season 2.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Gebbo's Bottomless Bag provides passive Intellect and a variety of different stat-based proc effects . Although this trinket is not particularly impressive for pure Single Target, its stat-based effects scale well into AoE, and it should be considered a top pick for most Season 2 content.

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone
items.guideNote: Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Wavecaller's Seastone is expected to be a solid overall passive trinket in both Raid and Mythic+ in Season 2, particularly shining in higher target counts where stat effects typically outscale direct damage.

items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance
items.guideNote: Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Fang of Umbral Malignance deals reasonable stacking damage in low target count situations, but truly shines in Mythic+ where the on-death effect provides substantial value. This trinket is particularly effective when chain-pulling mobs, as low-health mobs from the first pull will detonate and apply stacks to mobs from the second pull.

items.name: Vaelgor's Final Stare
items.guideNote: Vaelgor's Final Stare is a Season 1 trinket and cannot be obtained at a competitive item level in Season 2. The trinket's on-use Mastery effect was nerfed in pre-season tuning, but even afterwards this trinket at item level 298 remains particularly viable\u2014especially in Raids\u2014and is only outclassed by Season 2 trinkets on Myth track.

items.name: Vexhul's Everflowing Gland
items.guideNote: Vexhul's Everflowing Gland is a particularly strong on-use single-target damage effect, but is outscaled quickly when multiple targets are in play. That said, encounters with adds may trigger the cooldown reduction effect, providing quite a bit of additional value.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Freightrunner's Flask is one of the only on-use stat trinkets available in Season 2, providing Critical Strike on a 1.5 minute cooldown. While this effect is reasonably solid for raid encounters, this trinket is more likely to see use in Mythic+ for higher target counts.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: Lightspire Core is expected to be a solid overall passive trinket in both Raid and Mythic+ in Season 2, particularly shining in higher target counts where stat effects typically outscale direct damage. It should be noted that the bonus effect from this trinket always spawns on top of you, but do not expect to get full value from this effect every time it activates.

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: Containing a potent combination of static Critical Strike, on-use Agility every 90 seconds, bonus Physical damage to be amplified by your tier set and the Shado-Pan talents, and a potential Elevated Mythic item level, this trinket has everything a Brewmaster could want. Even on Heroic, it remains one of your strongest choices.

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: Although this trinket has an additional set effect when combined with Item #268209, its baseline 3ppm effect remains more than capable of dealing great damage. Not to mention, its damage being physical creates synergy with both the Shado-Pan Hero Talents and your tier set bonus, while also being available at the Elevated Mythic item level.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: The 4-minute cooldown of this trinket is steep, as is your inability to dodge attacks during its channel. However, this trinket makes up for it by decimating your foes in bursts of damage, both in single-target and AoE. It also is available at an Elevated Mythic item level.

items.name: Tumor of the Swarm
items.guideNote: While it may be a tank trinket, this item boasts surprisingly potent damage in addition to its stream of healing at a rate of 3ppm. Despite splitting its damage in AoE, the total amount dealt also increasing maintains its power as a passive and "hybrid" option across target counts.

items.name: Lustrous Golden Plumage
items.guideNote: What is likely to be your preferred on-use trinket if unable to access an Elevated Mythic Item #270175, this item grants you 20 seconds of increased Versatility every 2 minutes; this duration lines up nicely with Spell #132578 when used by Master of Harmony Brewmasters in particular.

items.name: Tiny Electromental in a Jar
items.guideNote: No less strong than it was in its Battle for Azeroth debut, this trinket's ability to gain roughly 20 charges per minute results in decent uptime of its AoE chain lightning effect which triggers every 12 charges accumulated. The scaling nature of this effect makes it useful across many target counts.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: This trinket's power is greater for Shado-Pan Brewmasters, whose shorter cooldown on Spell #132578 will readily line up with its on-demand Critical Strike every 90 seconds. However, it still remains incredibly potent for Master of Harmony players, too.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: There are six different effects this trinket can trigger, all at a rate of 3ppm: Spell #1292299 - 12-second self-bleed with a ramping Critical Strike bonus Spell #1308012 - 12-second Haste and movement speed buff Spell #1306870 - 12-second Mastery buff that decays over its duration Spell #1292300 - Versatility buff that decays with every ability used Spell #1308014 - Reduce all secondary stats for 12 seconds Spell #1308013 - Increase all secondary stats for 12 seconds While there may be a potential "bad" effect or two, these buffs are otherwise excellent and scale nicely across target counts. This easily makes it your strongest raid trinket among those that cannot reach the Elevated Mythic item level of 344.

items.name: Vashnik's Sanguine Rancor
items.guideNote: It may be a bit boring, but this trinket's damage, dealt roughly once per minute, has bonuses when striking either one enemy or multiple. This combines to make it a convenient passive choice, though you will feel a pang of regret if the damage doesn't line up when you want it to.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: You can see exceptional amounts of Mastery when wearing this trinket, but only if you are able to reliably stand in the light beams it creates, which may not always be possible in the middle of combat.

items.name: Keeper's Seething Core
items.guideNote: Despite being a Haste-focused trinket, this item performs surprisingly well for Brewmasters in the season largely due to its potential to scale your AoE damage in particular. It does so by reducing the cooldown of Spell #121253 to more regularly trigger your tier set bonuses; throw in a generous proc rate of 6ppm and you also frequently benefit from the 20% bonus to its Haste for having multiple stacks at once.

items.name: Ruby Whelp Shell
items.guideNote: There is a surprising amount of depth to the mechanics of this trinket, which greatly modifies its potential for players. This is due to there being 6 different effects that can occur; through training it over the course of a week to prioritize your desired buff you will gain a deceptively powerful item above its usual ranking. The 6 effects are: Spell #389839 - single-target damage Spell #390234 - AoE damage Spell #389820 - 12-second Haste buff Spell #383813 - 12-second Critical Strike buff Spell #390896 - single-target heal Spell #389818 - AoE heal It is recommended to train your whelp for AoE damage by activating its on-use while fighting AoE training dummies.

items.guideNote: While crafted Darkmoon Dominion trinkets quickly lose power as your item level increases due to their static value, they are uniquely enhanced in Midnight when worn with a crafted weapon using a matching Darkmoon Sigil embellishment (such as Item #245874). This can result in better performance than you would otherwise expect, but still won't reach the heights of the best-in-slot options.

items.name: Mindpiercer's Sigil

items.name: Wavecaller's Seastone

items.name: Vexhul's Everflowing Gland
items.guideNote: This is the best on use damage trinket available for this tier. This trinket will get some minor cooldown reduction on fights with adds which will help remain competitive on add fights despite doing pure single-target damage.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: This is a mastery proc trinket that provides a large boost to passive mastery, which is augmentations best stat. items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance

items.name: Fang of Umbral Malignance

icyveins.author: Sinzhu

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: With static Critical Strike, on-demand Agility every 90 seconds, bonus Physical damage that interacts with your tier set and the Shado-Pan talents, and an increased item level on Mythic, this trinket has absolutely everything you would want as a Brewmaster. Seek it out, even on Heroic.

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: While it may be part of a set effect with Aman'muso, Warlord's Vengeance, this trinket's baseline 3ppm effect is strong enough on its own to be a valuable pickup. The extra item level on Mythic certainly helps, too, as does its Physical damage being enhanced by both your tier set and the Shado-Pan Hero Talents.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: Its 4-minute cooldown is hefty, and you are unable to dodge attacks during its channel, but the damage output of this trinket is particularly exceptional in single-target. It is your strongest option for burst damage, especially at its Mythic item level of 344.

items.name: Tumor of the Swarm
items.guideNote: Although this is a tank trinket, its damage is surprisingly potent while also providing a helpful stream of healing at a rate of 3ppm. In spite of splitting its damage among enemies, the total amount dealt per proc also increases, making it an incredibly passive, "hybrid" option for AoE.

items.name: Lustrous Golden Plumage
items.guideNote: Perhaps your most useful on-use trinket if not able to receive "elevated" 344 options, this item provides a large burst of Versatility when you need for 20 seconds every 2 minutes. This lines up nicely with Invoke Niuzao, the Black Ox, but only for Master of Harmony Brewmasters.

items.name: Tiny Electromental in a Jar
items.guideNote: Still just as strong as it was in Battle for Azeroth, this trinket builds roughly 20 charges per minute and unleashes Nature damage with every 12 accumulated. By also including a chaining effect, it remains potent across a variety of target counts while being an option that is easy enough to obtain from Mythic+.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: This trinket is incredible for Shado-Pan players in particular, as its 90-second on-use cooldown for bonus Critical Strike lines up nicely with the reduced cooldown on Invoke Niuzao, the Black Ox available to this set of Hero Talents. However, Master of Harmony users will still find it quite potent.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Why? This trinket can trigger one of seven different effects at a rate of 3ppm:

items.name: Vashnik's Sanguine Rancor
items.guideNote: By offering benefits to its damage (triggering roughly once per minute) against only a single target and also against multiple, this trinket is a convenient universal and passive option for damage.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this trinket does provide a useful amount of Mastery, remember that you must be able to stand in its light beam to gain its full benefit; this may not always be feasible in the middle of combat.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: (Crit)

items.name: Keeper's Seething Core
items.guideNote: You may be wondering how a trinket with Haste can be placed so highly. This is largely because of the stat's potential to scale with your AoE damage in particular, while also triggering more applications of your 4-set bonus by helping to reduce the cooldown of Keg Smash. And, with a generous proc rate of 6 per minute, you will frequently trigger the 20% bonus effect as well!

items.name: Ruby Whelp Shell
items.guideNote: Why? Much of this trinket's value depends on how you take advantage of the ability to "train" the whelp it spawns over the course of a week. By doing so, you can have it properly prioritize one of the following effects approximately once per minute:

items.name: Darkmoon Dominion: Void
items.guideNote: While this trinket can only be obtained at a static item level and will quickly be outscaled by "worse" alternatives, it is enhanced if paired with a crafted weapon featuring a matching embellishment ( Darkmoon Sigil: Void).

items.guideNote: This trinket is surprisingly strong for having an effect similar to alchemist stones of every prior expansion. However, in Midnight this item counts as an embellished piece of gear, making it difficult to justify.

items.name: Voracious Heart of Ula'tek
items.guideNote: This is by far the best on-use option available in Season 2, despite being on an awkward 1m30s cooldown. No other option comes close in power, so this is one of your big chase items. Always hold it to line up with your Ascendance or Surging Totem window.

items.name: Zul'jin's Guillotine Technique
items.guideNote: A stock-standard direct damage trinket, but gets stronger when paired with the cantrip weapon, Aman'muso, Warlord's Vengeance. This has less uses in AoE content, but for single-target and especially cleave within the raid it's the strongest passive option available.

items.name: Vile Vial of Volatile Venom
items.guideNote: Definitely not as strong as Voracious Heart, but a good alternative if you're in need of an on-use. When using it and Potion of Recklessness together, make sure to pot before activating this to avoid increasing the wrong stat.

items.name: Gebbo's Bottomless Bag
items.guideNote: Triggers a variety of different stat boosting effects, and different buffs can overlap. While it does have a negative proc in the pool, it's the best passive stat option available, making it a good pick for AoE heavy encounters and dungeons.

items.name: Void Execution Mandate
items.guideNote: Try to always use this on a target that will live long enough for you to stack up the Crit buff, else most of its value is lost.

items.name: Freightrunner's Flask
items.guideNote: Hold to line up with Ascendance / Surging Totem depending on build. When using Potion of Recklessness, make sure to pot before using your trinket to avoid setting it to Crit.

items.name: Lightspire Core
items.guideNote: While this is tuned well and Mastery is desirable, staying within the zone of the proc is extremely restrictive, especially in Season 2. Due to both the large arenas in raid encounters and the hectic movement in dungeons, your mileage may vary in reality when using it.

items.name: Drum of Renewed Bonds
items.guideNote: Go to the Jan'alai altar in Zul'Aman to set this to Mastery.

items.name: Font of Venomous Rage
items.guideNote: This deals an extremely large amount of burst damage to your primary target when used, alongside some bonus AoE. While it struggles against other options due to it being a channel and a long cooldown, it's unique potential to be useful to deal with key enemies means it might be worth looking at in certain edge cases in Season 2.

Ideal usage of this trinket is to train it 4 times in the crit buff (target yourself when standing alone) and 2 times in the haste buff (target yourself when standing amongst a group of allies). It allows you a flexible damage amp to utilize wherever you want, and thus can be powerful in certain situations, especially so if you are playing Annihilator. The downside of losing primary stat is very real however, and keeps this from being a blanket recommendation.

While this trinket looks good on paper, and sims quite well, the trinket itself is nearly impossible to get full value out of by standing in it's beam. Additionally, the proc of the beam can cancel your Void Ray should it proc while channeling, making this trinket incredibly bad untill that is fixed. Stay away from this trinket untill then.

The best passive trinket from the raid. It has the chance to proc 6 different buffs, and buffs can overlap. Some of them are negative effects, but are massively outweighed by the positive effect procs.

This trinket and the Gebbo's Bottomless Bag are very close in power, and whichever one you decide to use depends on what drops for you. There can be differences between the trinkets based on talents, but you should sim them opposite each other to figure out which one to use.

2 minute trinket from Mythic+. Currently the best simming on-use trinket available. Alters your cooldown planning a little to accomodate the cooldown. This trinket can alter which stat you get from Potion of Recklessness if you are using that, so remember to press the Potion before the trinket!
90 second trinket from Mythic+. Gives a decent Critical Strike buff when used. Alters your cooldown planning a little to accomodate the cooldown.
Solid passive trinket alternative from Mythic+. Potentially strong if you manage to stand inside the light zone.

Guilotine is a simple trinket, it's just a damage proc however it's tuned strong enough that it's our strongest option in single target.

Very Strong Trinket for DPS
An extremely powerful healing trinket in both raid and dungeon.
A solid Haste / Intellect stat stick. Available off the new Lair boss.
Despite featuring weaker stats for us, this is a good starter trinket since it is acquirable without stepping foot in a raid or dungeon.

Recommended for Raid. Font of Venomous Rage is a powerful burst damage trinket providing massive on-use single-target damage on a long 4-minute cooldown. This trinket can be obtained at item level 344 from Mythic Ula'tek and is currently the strongest trinket available for pure Single Target, particularly if burst damage is valuable or required. That said, this trinket does not scale as well as stat trinkets when it comes to buffing allies in sustained AoE encounters, and there are few encounters in Season 2 with a pure single-target damage profile.

Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Mindpiercer's Sigil is a passive trinket with no baseline stats, instead providing direct damage and an Intellect proc. This trinket loses some value in high target counts, but on average is one of the strongest trinkets available for Augmentation in Season 2.

Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Gebbo's Bottomless Bag provides passive Intellect and a variety of different stat-based proc effects . Although this trinket is not particularly impressive for pure Single Target, its stat-based effects scale well into AoE, and it should be considered a top pick for most Season 2 content.

Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Wavecaller's Seastone is expected to be a solid overall passive trinket in both Raid and Mythic+ in Season 2, particularly shining in higher target counts where stat effects typically outscale direct damage.

Recommended for Raid and Mythic+. Fang of Umbral Malignance deals reasonable stacking damage in low target count situations, but truly shines in Mythic+ where the on-death effect provides substantial value. This trinket is particularly effective when chain-pulling mobs, as low-health mobs from the first pull will detonate and apply stacks to mobs from the second pull.

Vaelgor's Final Stare is a Season 1 trinket and cannot be obtained at a competitive item level in Season 2. The trinket's on-use Mastery effect was nerfed in pre-season tuning, but even afterwards this trinket at item level 298 remains particularly viable\u2014especially in Raids\u2014and is only outclassed by Season 2 trinkets on Myth track.

Vexhul's Everflowing Gland is a particularly strong on-use single-target damage effect, but is outscaled quickly when multiple targets are in play. That said, encounters with adds may trigger the cooldown reduction effect, providing quite a bit of additional value.

Freightrunner's Flask is one of the only on-use stat trinkets available in Season 2, providing Critical Strike on a 1.5 minute cooldown. While this effect is reasonably solid for raid encounters, this trinket is more likely to see use in Mythic+ for higher target counts.

Lightspire Core is expected to be a solid overall passive trinket in both Raid and Mythic+ in Season 2, particularly shining in higher target counts where stat effects typically outscale direct damage. It should be noted that the bonus effect from this trinket always spawns on top of you, but do not expect to get full value from this effect every time it activates.
Passive Trinket. Overall Best.

Passive trinket. Second best raid option.

An extremely heavy hitter that dominates both raid and mythic+ selections. Drops off the first boss so should be obtainable by most people - even if Raid isn't really your bag.
While this loses to a lot of Myth-track alternatives, it's extremely easy to get and punches well above its item level.

Best-in-slot for Mythic+ and one of the best options in raid. Provides solid burst. The main downside is you're not gonna have this available at max item level for a while.
This is a potential sleeper hit trinket, which is very fight dependent. Save it if you obtain it! Use alongside Item #271887.
This is generally gonna be your best option from Mythic+, as it provides solid burst on top of a de facto damage reduciton.

There are six different effects this trinket can trigger, all at a rate of 3ppm: Spell #1292299 - 12-second self-bleed with a ramping Critical Strike bonus Spell #1308012 - 12-second Haste and movement speed buff Spell #1306870 - 12-second Mastery buff that decays over its duration Spell #1292300 - Versatility buff that decays with every ability used Spell #1308014 - Reduce all secondary stats for 12 seconds Spell #1308013 - Increase all secondary stats for 12 seconds While there may be a potential "bad" effect or two, these buffs are otherwise excellent and scale nicely across target counts. This easily makes it your strongest raid trinket among those that cannot reach the Elevated Mythic item level of 344.

Despite being a Haste-focused trinket, this item performs surprisingly well for Brewmasters in the season largely due to its potential to scale your AoE damage in particular. It does so by reducing the cooldown of Spell #121253 to more regularly trigger your tier set bonuses; throw in a generous proc rate of 6ppm and you also frequently benefit from the 20% bonus to its Haste for having multiple stacks at once.

There is a surprising amount of depth to the mechanics of this trinket, which greatly modifies its potential for players. This is due to there being 6 different effects that can occur; through training it over the course of a week to prioritize your desired buff you will gain a deceptively powerful item above its usual ranking.
